passage: Kishore, you asked why I never call Vinod. Your uncle Chetan has an old story about that. Sit. When I was fifteen, I thought Vinod had forgotten my birthday. I said nothing. I stopped answering his notes, moved to the back bench and took the other road home. I told myself, if he cares, he will ask. He did ask, once, and I looked at my shoes. Vinod decided I was angry about the science project partner he had picked, which was not it at all. He stopped asking. By Diwali we nodded in the corridor like strangers, and the weeks turned into a habit. Last year, forty years on, I met Vinod at a wedding, and he still believed it was about the science project. I never told him about the birthday.

qa.q: Where did Chetan sit after he stopped answering Vinod's notes?
qa.a: Chetan moved to the back bench.

qa.q: What did Chetan hope for by staying silent, and what feeling sat behind it?
qa.a: Chetan hoped Vinod would notice and ask, feeling hurt and proud about the birthday he thought had been forgotten.

qa.q: What could the young Chetan have done when Vinod asked, and why?
qa.a: Chetan could have said that the birthday hurt, because one honest sentence would have replaced Vinod's wrong guess about the science project.

qa.q: How did Vinod read Chetan's silence?
qa.a: Vinod read it as rejection and guessed it was about the science project partner, so Vinod stopped asking and the distance hardened.

grounding: The student stops replying and sits elsewhere hoping the problem disappears, the friend takes it as rejection and guesses the cause wrongly, and the distance hardens over weeks.

passage: Abhinav had laughed when the teacher read out Avni's poem, and Avni had felt her face go hot. She didn't say anything. She just stopped replying to his messages and moved to the window seat, away from him. The trouble was the school bus: forty minutes each way, every day, with Abhinav three rows ahead. On the first day he turned round twice. By the end of the week he had stopped turning. Avni heard from a friend that Abhinav thought she was angry because he had joined the cricket team and had less time. That wasn't it at all. But explaining now felt harder than staying silent. By the third week they sat on the same bus like strangers, and the poem was the smallest part of it.

qa.q: How long was the school bus ride?
qa.a: Forty minutes each way, every day.

qa.q: Why did Avni stay silent even after hearing Abhinav's guess?
qa.a: She felt embarrassed and stuck; explaining felt harder than staying silent, even though his guess was wrong.

qa.q: What could Avni have said on the first day?
qa.a: Something simple like "It hurt when you laughed at my poem", which would have stopped Abhinav guessing wrongly.

qa.q: How did Abhinav seem to read Avni's silence?
qa.a: He seemed to take it as rejection, turning round at first and then giving up, and wrongly blamed it on joining the cricket team.

grounding: Shows a student going silent instead of talking, the friend guessing the wrong cause, and distance hardening over weeks.

passage: When Mohit picked two other boys for the inter-school quiz team instead of him, Divyansh didn't argue. He just stopped. Stopped replying on the chat, stopped waiting at the gate of their building in Indore, took the long way to tuition. He told himself it would blow over. Mohit messaged: "You okay?" Then: "Is this about my birthday? I said sorry about that." Then nothing. Divyansh read every message and answered none. By the second week Mohit had started walking with the quiz boys. By the fourth, Divyansh saw them laughing in the canteen and felt something tighten in his chest. He still hadn't said a word about the quiz. Now it felt too late to start.

qa.q: What did Mohit guess the silence was about?
qa.a: Mohit's birthday, which Mohit had said sorry about.

qa.q: What did Divyansh feel seeing Mohit laugh in the canteen?
qa.a: He felt hurt and left out, something tightening in his chest, and regretful that it now felt too late to talk.

qa.q: What would have worked better than going silent?
qa.a: Telling Mohit early that being left off the quiz team hurt, so Mohit wouldn't have to guess and the distance couldn't harden.

qa.q: How might Mohit feel after the messages go unanswered?
qa.a: Mohit may feel confused and rejected, guessing the wrong reason, and eventually drifts toward new friends.

grounding: Shows a student avoiding a friend in silence, the friend guessing wrongly, and the gap hardening over several weeks.
